semantic_changes: After each restart the harness disconnects the restarted node from every peer, samples its state for one second, and emits an '<name>_isolated' event with the configured server count, whether campaigning was observed, the term before and after, and the final state.
Four comparisons are added over the two isolated events.

scope.description: The two restart modes of the no-snapshot fixture, each followed by isolating the restarted node from its peers for one second to see whether a node with an empty configuration campaigns.
assumptions: The isolation is expressed by disconnecting the restarted node from every peer, so it hears no heartbeat and its heartbeat timer fires within the observation window (the configured heartbeat timeout is 50ms and the window is one second).
The observation is a sample of the node's state every 5ms; campaigning is recorded as observed if the state was ever candidate or leader during the window.
The term is recorded as an operand: with pre-vote active a candidate does not increment its term until a pre-vote succeeds, so the term is not used as a predicate.
The empty configuration and the bootstrap configuration come from the same restart events recorded in the previous receipt; this experiment repeats them so its own receipt carries the operands.
excluded: No votes are solicited from real peers, so this does not execute an election outcome for either mode.
No snapshot failure or crash is injected.

basis.prefix: The harness builds three in-memory transports in a full mesh with per-node in-memory stores, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts the three nodes with MockFSM, elects B as leader, applies ten commands, takes no snapshot on A and emits a 'fixture' event. It then shuts A down and restarts it twice from its own stores, once with the feature enabled and once without it, emitting 'restart_with_feature' and 'restart_without_feature' with the returned flag, state, last applied index, reported configuration and its length. Immediately after each restart the harness disconnects A from B and C, samples A's state every 5ms for one second, and emits '<name>_isolated' with the configured server count, whether candidate or leader state was ever observed, whether the term advanced, the term before and after, and the final state. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart_with_feature, restart_with_feature_isolated, restart_without_feature, restart_without_feature_isolated.
basis.responsibility: hashicorp/raft follower election gate and the pre-vote extension: the gate refuses to campaign while the latest configuration index is zero, and a campaigning node runs a pre-vote before incrementing its term.

comparisons.description: Feature on: the restarted node's configuration should be empty, so the isolation is exercised against that state.
Feature on: an isolated node whose configuration is empty should not campaign, keeping the consequence contained.
Feature off control: the same isolation applied to a node holding the bootstrap membership.
Feature off control: with a configuration the isolated node should campaign, so the isolation is a real trigger.

before.description: Live three-node cluster {A,B,C} in which node A runs with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, receives ten committed commands plus the bootstrap configuration entry and takes no snapshot at all, is shut down and then restarted twice from its own stores: once with the feature enabled and once without it.
assumptions: All state comes from normal operations: bootstrap {A,B,C} from A, election with leadership moved to B so A is a follower, ten committed applies and a graceful shutdown of A.
A takes no snapshot because the harness never snapshots it and SnapshotInterval is ten minutes, so A's snapshot store is empty at the restart.
A's log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore and stages a commit index while O is running with the feature enabled, so the replay has entries to cover.
The reported configuration is read through the node's atomic latest-configuration copy after each restart, with a 300ms settle.
Exact indexes are reported as operands but not asserted; the admission pins the absence of snapshots, the running node's configuration and the number of committed commands.
excluded: No crash, on-disk store, or snapshot failure is injected; the node simply has no snapshot.
An election by the restarted node is not attempted, so the source-derived consequence that it will not campaign is not executed.

prefix.before: The harness builds three InmemTransports (A, B, C) in a full mesh with per-node InmemStore, InmemCommitTrackingStore and InmemSnapshotStore, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts A, B and C with MockFSM, waits for a leader and transfers leadership to B so A stays a follower. It applies ten commands on B, waits until A's log store reports a staged commit index, takes no snapshot on A, and emits a 'fixture' event with the number of snapshots A holds, A's staged commit index, its log last index, the configuration A reports while running, the leader and the number of committed commands. It then shuts A down and restarts it in a goroutine from its own stores with a fresh transport, twice in sequence: 'restart_with_feature' with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and 'restart_without_feature' with it disabled, each emitting newraft_returned, the node state, last applied index, the reported configuration id list and its length, and the number of voters in the log's configuration entry. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart_with_feature, restart_without_feature.
prefix.after: The harness builds three in-memory transports in a full mesh with per-node in-memory stores, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, starts the three nodes with MockFSM, elects B as leader, applies ten commands, takes no snapshot on A and emits a 'fixture' event. It then shuts A down and restarts it twice from its own stores, once with the feature enabled and once without it, emitting 'restart_with_feature' and 'restart_without_feature' with the returned flag, state, last applied index, reported configuration and its length. Immediately after each restart the harness disconnects A from B and C, samples A's state every 5ms for one second, and emits '<name>_isolated' with the configured server count, whether candidate or leader state was ever observed, whether the term advanced, the term before and after, and the final state. All nodes are shut down afterwards. Event order: fixture, restart_with_feature, restart_with_feature_isolated, restart_without_feature, restart_without_feature_isolated.
